What is Speechify?

Primarily a text-to-speech reader that converts documents, web pages, PDFs and emails into spoken audio for consumption - with a separate Speechify Studio product for producing voiceovers and dubbing.

Best for

Listening to documents and web content rather than reading them.

Main features

  • Read-aloud across web, PDF, Word, EPUB, scanned documents (with OCR) and physical text via phone camera
  • speeds up to 4.5x
  • 200+ voices in 60+ languages including celebrity-licensed voices
  • highlighting synchronised with speech
  • Speechify Studio for voiceover, dubbing and video
  • voice cloning
  • Chrome extension reading any page
  • offline listening
  • note-taking and summarisation.

Practical use cases

  • Listening to research papers or long reports while commuting
  • accessibility support for dyslexic readers
  • getting through a heavy email and document load
  • converting a PDF textbook into audio
  • producing a video voiceover in Studio.

Who is it for?

  • People with dyslexia, ADHD or visual impairment; students; commuters; professionals with heavy reading loads; content producers via Studio.

Pricing, free access & limits

Freemium consumer subscription; separate Studio product; education and enterprise licensing

Plans described in the source

Free with basic voices and limited speed. Speechify Premium around $139/yr (roughly $11.58/mo) for 200+ voices, 60+ languages, high-quality voices and unlimited listening. Speechify Studio priced separately, roughly $24-29/mo billed annually for voiceover and dubbing production. Education and Enterprise licensing quoted per organisation. Monthly billing is available at a substantial premium over annual.

Free plan

Yes - free tier with basic voices and standard reading speeds.

Free trial

Yes - 3-day or 7-day Premium trials commonly offered; note the auto-renew into an annual plan, which generates frequent billing complaints.

Usage limits to consider

Free tier restricts voice selection, reading speed and some formats. Studio is metered by generation minutes. Celebrity voices are subject to licensing and availability changes.

Strengths & tradeoffs

These points summarize the supplied research, rather than hands-on test results.

Strengths noted in the source

  • Best-in-class as an accessibility and consumption tool - the OCR-plus-camera reading of physical text is genuinely valuable for dyslexic users
  • extremely broad platform coverage
  • speed control up to 4.5x transforms reading throughput for heavy readers
  • strong education licensing programmes.

Limitations to consider

  • Two quite different products under one brand causes confusion at purchase
  • the trial-to-annual auto-renewal is aggressive and generates a high volume of billing complaints - read the terms carefully
  • Studio's production quality is below ElevenLabs and Murf
  • Arabic listening voices are limited
  • pricing presentation is misleading (annual rate shown as a monthly figure).

Platforms, languages & integrations

Platforms

  • Web, iOS, Android, macOS, Chrome/Edge/Safari extensions, Microsoft Word add-in

Languages

  • 60+ languages including Arabic and French for listening

API access

Yes - Speechify API for text-to-speech, priced by characters

Integrations and exports

  • Chrome, Google Docs, Gmail, Canvas LMS, Microsoft Word, Dropbox, Google Drive, Kindle (via export)

Evaluation notes

Read the auto-renewal terms before starting a trial - this is the most common complaint about the product and the annual charge is substantial. For production voiceover rather than listening, Studio is not the strongest option in this group.
